newsitem.title: ITALY: MOTOR RACING-LUCKLESS BERGER CRASHES ON RETURN.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR RACING-LUCKLESS BERGER CRASHES ON RETURN.

text.p: Luckless Austrian Formula One driver Gerhard Berger crashed at Monza on Wednesday during his first outing for Benetton since he underwent a sinus operation in May.
Berger, who also suffered the death of his father in a plane crash last week, sped off the Italian Grand Prix circuit at 300 kph during a test session.
"It could have been a horrible accident but luckily I ended up on the grass and everything was alright," he said. "But it certainly wasn't a great return."

Berger, who has missed the last three grands prix in Montreal, Magny Cours and Silverstone due to sinus problems, said he had no intention of retiring when his contract with Italian team Benetton ran out at the end of the season.
"I'm a driver and I want to keep on racing," he said, adding that he had held talks with the Williams team and expected to continue driving for at least two more seasons.
Berger considered retirement after the deaths of compatriot Roland Ratzenberger and Brazilian three-time world champion Ayrton Senna at the 1994 San Marino Grand Prix.
